chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed, then gave the salām in two rak'at. So one behind him asked him, 'O Messenger of Allah! Did something new occur in the prayer?' He said: 'And what is that?' They said, 'You only prayed two rak'at.' So he said: 'Was it like that, O Zal al-Yadayn?' And he used to be called Zal al-Shimalayn. So he said: 'Yes'. So he built upon his prayer and completed the prayer with four (rak'at).

And he (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah is the One who caused him to forget as a mercy for the community. Do you not see that if a man were to do this, he would be faulted and it would be said, 'Your prayer is not accepted'? So whoever enters upon him today, that one says, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established a Sunnah and it became an example, and he performed two prostrations for the sake of the speech.'

key_terms.ذَا الْيَدَيْنِ: Zal al-Yadayn (The Possessor of the Two Hands, a title for the Prophet)
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: gave the salām (concluding greeting of prayer)
key_terms.لِمَكَانِ الْكَلَامِ: for the sake of the speech/interruption

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi records the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) pausing his prayer to converse with Mu'adh ibn Jabal, resulting in a shortened two-rak'ah prayer that he later completed to four. The narration highlights the principle of 'Nasi'ah' (divine forgetfulness) as a mercy to the Ummah, establishing that speaking during prayer does not invalidate it but requires completing the missed portion. This incident serves as a foundational legal precedent in Shia jurisprudence for the validity of Salāt despite minor interruptions or speech.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Nu’man, from Saeed Al A’araj who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Send Blessings upon Rasool-Allahazwj, then offer Salām in the two Rak’at. So the one behind himsaww asked himsaww, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! Did something new occurred regarding the Salāt?’ Hesaww said: ‘And what is that?’ They said, ‘But rather yousaww prayed two Rak’at’. So hesaww said: ‘Was it like that, O Zal Yadaeyn?’ And he used to be called Zal Shimaleyn. So he said, ‘Yes’. So hesaww built upon hissaww Salāt, and completed the Salāt with four (Rak’at)’.

And heasws said: ‘Allahazwj, Heazwj is the Oneazwj Who Cause himsaww to omit as a Mercy for the community. Do you not see that if a man were to do this he would be faulted and it would be said, ‘Your Salāt is not Acceptable’? So the one upon whom that enters, it would be said, ‘Rasool-Allahsaww had established a Sunnah and has become an example, and perform Sajdah two Sujūd in place of the speech (for talking)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Sa‘id al-‘A’raj who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘The Messenger of Allah once said Salam (the phrase of offering greeting of peace) in two Rak‘at and those behind him asked, “O Messenger of Allah, has something happened to Salah (prayer)?” The Messenger of Allah asked, “Why is that?” They replied, “You performed only two Rak‘at.” The Messenger of Allah then asked, “Was it so, O Dhu al- Yadayn?” - he was also called Dhu al-Shamalayn - He replied, “Yes, it was so.” The Messenger of Allah based his Salah (prayer) on that and completed it as four Rak‘at.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah made him to forget to grant and make it a mercy for the nation (his followers). Is it not true that if a man does so, he is reproached and is told that his Salah (prayer) is not accepted? If today someone experiences such condition he says that the Messenger of Allah has established a Sunnah (tradition) and it has become a guideline to follow. He (the Messenger of Allah) then performed two Sajdah (prostration) because of speaking.’”
